brief: Core PCE rose 3.0% y/y in August, 0.7pp above GS's 2.3% start-of-year forecast. GS decomposes the overshoot to judge whether it reflects one-off shocks or broader stickiness. Consumer electronics, mainly computer software and accessories, add over 0.3pp from AI-driven demand, but GS estimates 0.1pp of that is mismeasurement: the PCE weight for software is roughly 30x its CPI weight and the component isn't quality-adjusted for new AI features, so the contribution should ease in 2027 as memory-price effects fade. Air transportation adds 0.2pp from Iran-war-driven jet fuel costs; energy passthrough overall adds 0.3pp and tariff passthrough adds 0.1pp, concentrated in the other core goods component, where GS's updated model now assumes 80% peak passthrough (up from 70% assumed in January), though a lower effective tariff rate after the Supreme Court's IEEPA ruling offsets most of that increase. Shelter adds 0.1pp. Pharmaceuticals (Medicare negotiations, TrumpRx) and used vehicles subtract a combined 0.2pp, durably. GS concludes roughly three-fourths of the surprise is transitory or mismeasurement, leaving only about 0.2pp of genuine upside concentrated in housing and other AI-exposed electronics, and keeps its forecast for core PCE to fall to 2.2% by December 2027.

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: Core PCE inflation was 3.0% year over year in August, 0.7pp above Goldman's 2.3% start-of-year forecast for the month.
cards.anchor: Core PCE stood at 3.0% year over year in August, 0.7pp above our 2.3% start-of-the-year forecast for August.

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: Computer software and accessories and other electronics are responsible for more than 0.3pp of the core PCE overshoot, reflecting a larger-than-expected AI-related boost to consumer prices.
cards.anchor: Computer software and accessories and other electronics are responsible for more than 0.3pp of the overshoot, reflecting a larger-than-expected AI-related boost to consumer prices.

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: Computer software and accessories still contributes 0.2pp to the core PCE surprise even after recent methodological changes, and Goldman believes that contribution overstates the underlying price impulse.
cards.anchor: computer software and accessories still contributes 0.2pp, and we think that contribution overstates the underlying price impulse for two reasons.

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: The computer software and accessories component's weight in PCE is roughly 30 times its CPI weight because PCE source data overstates software sales to retail customers.
cards.anchor: its weight is too high—roughly 30 times the CPI weight—because the PCE source data overstates software sales to retail customers.

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: The computer software and accessories component is not quality-adjusted like other technology components, so new AI features have likely been captured as price increases rather than quantity increases.
cards.anchor: the component is not quality-adjusted like other technology components, so new AI features have likely been captured as price increases rather than quantity increases.

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: Goldman estimates that overweighting and the lack of quality adjustment together currently overstate the consumer electronics contribution to core PCE by 0.1pp.
cards.anchor: Together, we estimate these factors currently overstate the consumer electronics contribution by 0.1pp.

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: Goldman expects the fading impact of the memory price shock to reduce the software and accessories component's contribution to core PCE over the next year.
cards.anchor: We also expect that the fading impact of the memory price shock will reduce the contribution of this component over the next year.

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: Air transportation accounts for another 0.2pp of the core PCE surprise, largely reflecting higher jet fuel prices from the war with Iran.
cards.anchor: Air transportation accounts for another 0.2pp surprise, largely reflecting higher jet fuel prices from the war with Iran.

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: Energy cost passthrough to air transportation and other components accounts for 0.3pp of the core PCE surprise.
cards.anchor: we estimate that energy cost passthrough to air transportation and other components accounts for 0.3pp of the surprise

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: The other core goods component of core PCE was worth 0.1pp of the surprise, roughly a third of which is related to greater-than-expected tariff passthrough.
cards.anchor: The other core goods component was worth 0.1pp, roughly a third of which is related to greater-than-expected tariff passthrough.

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: Goldman's updated tariff passthrough model puts peak consumer price passthrough at 80%, above the 70% it assumed in January.
cards.anchor: An update to our tariff passthrough model puts the peak consumer price passthrough at 80%, above the 70% we assumed in January

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: The higher tariff passthrough assumption has been largely offset by the decline in the effective tariff rate after the Supreme Court's ruling on the IEEPA tariffs.
cards.anchor: the higher passthrough has been largely offset by the decline in the effective tariff rate after the Supreme Court ruling on the IEEPA tariffs

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: Shelter inflation added roughly 0.1pp to the upside surprise in core PCE because it slowed by less than Goldman expected.
cards.anchor: Shelter inflation added roughly 0.1pp to the upside surprise because it slowed by less than expected.

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: Goldman continues to expect further disinflation in shelter in the coming months.
cards.anchor: we continue to expect further disinflation in this category in the coming months.

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: Pharmaceuticals and used vehicles subtracted a combined 0.2pp from core PCE relative to Goldman's forecast.
cards.anchor: pharmaceuticals and used vehicles subtracted a combined 0.2pp relative to our forecast.

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: Goldman views the downside surprises in pharmaceuticals and used vehicles as durable price level changes that are unlikely to reverse.
cards.anchor: We see both downside surprises as durable price level changes that are unlikely to reverse.

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: The decline in pharmaceutical prices reflects Medicare drug price negotiations and the launch of the TrumpRx discount program.
cards.anchor: The decline in pharmaceutical prices reflects the implementation of Medicare drug price negotiations, the launch of the TrumpRx discount program

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: The softening in used vehicle prices is likely due to an unwinding of H2 2025 increases, when CPI outpaced wholesale prices.
cards.anchor: The softening in used vehicle prices is likely due to an unwinding of its H2 2025 increases when CPI outpaced wholesale prices

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: The temporary boost to core PCE from the oil shock, tariffs, and the software and accessories component accounts for roughly three-fourths of the inflation surprise and should ease over the next year.
cards.anchor: accounts for roughly three-fourths of the surprise and should ease throughout the next year

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: Goldman estimates approximately 0.2pp of genuine upside remains in core PCE, most of it from housing and other AI-exposed electronics.
cards.anchor: This leaves approximately 0.2pp of genuine upside, most of which comes from housing and other AI-exposed electronics.

cards.document: US Daily: Where Has Inflation Surprised?
cards.claim: Goldman does not read the core PCE overshoot as evidence of a meaningful acceleration in the underlying inflation trend relative to its start-of-year forecast.
